chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah, from al-Qāsim ibn Burayd, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام:

Regarding a man who prayed two rakʿahs of the obligatory salat (prayer), then gave salām while thinking that he had completed the salat (prayer), and spoke, then remembered that he had not prayed more than two rakʿahs, he said: “He completes what remains of his salat (prayer), and there is nothing upon him.”

So this does not contradict what we mentioned regarding the obligation of the two sajdahs of forgetfulness upon him, because in these two reports it is not stated that the two sajdahs of forgetfulness are not upon him. Rather, he only said, “There is nothing upon him,” and it is possible that by that he indicated something other than that, such as burden and sin and what is of their kind.

key_terms.سَجْدَتَيِ السَّهْوِ: the two prostrations required for forgetfulness in salat (prayer)
key_terms.فَسَلَّمَ: he gave the concluding salām of salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone gives salām after two rakʿahs of an obligatory salat (prayer), speaks, and then realizes the prayer was incomplete?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of one who mistakenly ends an obligatory salat (prayer) after two rakʿahs, speaks, and then remembers that the prayer was incomplete. The ruling given is that he completes the remaining part of the salat (prayer), while the compiler clarifies that this does not negate the obligation of sajdatay al-sahw, since the phrase “nothing is upon him” may mean no sin or blame.
